ic_name: DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface, IEC 62386 via TI SLAA422A)
document_title: Digital Addressable Lighting Interface (DALI) Implementation Using MSP430 Value Line Microcontrollers — Application Report SLAA422A
manufacturer: Texas Instruments Incorporated (application report). DALI itself is standardized by IEC TC 34 in the IEC 62386 series (originally IEC 60929 Annex E); the protocol is overseen by the DALI Alliance / DiiA.
copyright: © 2009-2012, Texas Instruments Incorporated. DALI is overseen by the DALI Alliance (DiiA) and standardized by the IEC 62386 multi-part series.
abstract: The Digital Addressable Lighting Interface (DALI) was defined in IEC 60929 and has been updated in IEC 62386 (one of the main reasons for the update was the inclusion of the LED device type — IEC 62386-209 and the dedicated LED-driver part 207). DALI is a half-duplex digital communication composed of forward and backward frames. Forward frames (control device → control gear) consist of one start bit, one address byte, one data byte, and two stop bits (16 bits transmitted on the wire). Backward frames (the response after reception of a query or memory command in the forward frame, control gear → control device) consist of one start bit, one data byte, and two stop bits. DALI uses Manchester encoding at 1200 baud. The voltage of the interface power supply can vary from 11.5 V to 22.5 V per the standard (DC bus, polarity-insensitive at receivers, current-limited to 250 mA). This TI application report implements a DALI LED device-type control gear on the TPS62260LED-338 EVM with an MSP430F2131 microcontroller (and, in Appendix B, an MSP430G2xx2 value-line device on the Launchpad MSP-EXP430G2). The MSP430F2131 performs the DALI communication (CPU-software Manchester encode/decode) while the Timer_A3 module updates the LED-driving PWMs and the Watchdog Timer Plus (WDT+) implements DALI-mandated fade timing and configuration-command flash housekeeping.
external_pins: DALI is a standardized lighting-control protocol, not a chip; the bus itself is a 2-wire DC interface (commonly labeled DA / DA+ and DA- or D+ and D-) that is polarity-insensitive at receivers.
On the TI application report hardware the DALI line is opto-isolated from the MSP430. From the MSP430 side the relevant pins are:
DALI_RX — input (P2.0 on both MSP430F2131 and MSP430G2xx2); interrupt-on-edge, used by the CPU to Manchester-decode the incoming forward frame.
DALI_TX — output (P2.1 on both implementations); used by the CPU to drive the bus (through the opto-isolator) when sending a backward frame.
PWM1 — output (P1.2/TA1 on F2131; P1.6/TA0.1 on G2xx2) — Timer_A3 PWM compare-output driving an LED.
PWM2 — output (P1.3/TA2 on F2131; P1.4/TA0.2 on G2xx2) — second LED PWM.
TPS62260_ENABLE — output (P1.0 on F2131; P1.1 on G2xx2) — gates the TPS62260 LED-driver buck.
VCC / GND — MSP430 supply (3.3 V typical) and ground.
EZ430 RF2500 / Launchpad / programmer connector — for in-circuit programming / debug.
package: Not a packaged silicon part. DALI is published as the IEC 62386 multi-part international standard (originally IEC 60929 Annex E, 1999). The TI implementation runs on the MSP430F2131 (TSSOP-20 / PDIP-20) and MSP430G2xx2 value-line Launchpad devices (PDIP-14/20, TSSOP-14/20).

supported_transports.name: DALI 2-wire DC bus
supported_transports.physical_layer: Two-wire, polarity-insensitive at the receiver, DC voltage 9.5 V..22.5 V across the bus (TI application report cites 11.5 V..22.5 V per the standard); bus current limited to typically 250 mA.
supported_transports.duplex: Half-duplex — only one device transmits at a time; control device sends forward frame, addressed control gear may answer with a backward frame.
supported_transports.adu_size_bits: 16 (forward frame) / 8 (backward frame); on the wire 19 bit-times of Manchester (1 start + 16 data + 2 stop) for forward; 11 bit-times (1 start + 8 data + 2 stop) for backward.
supported_transports.adu_format: Forward: START + Address byte (YAAAAAAB) + Data byte + 2 stop bits. Backward: START + Data byte + 2 stop bits.
supported_transports.framing: Manchester (bi-phase) encoding at 1200 baud (half-bit-time TE = 416.67 μs); idle = bus HIGH (active level); two stop bits = continuous HIGH for ≥ 2 × TE.

modes_of_operation.name: DALI Idle
modes_of_operation.description: Bus idle (HIGH). Control gear waits for a forward-frame start bit (1→0 transition halfway through the bit time).

modes_of_operation.name: Forward-frame reception
modes_of_operation.description: Control gear samples the Manchester-encoded forward frame, decodes Address byte (YAAAAAAB) + Data byte, validates address, and queues the command for execution.

modes_of_operation.name: Forward-frame execution
modes_of_operation.description: Execute the decoded direct-arc-power command (B=0) or indirect command (B=1) — change Actual Level, run a fade routine, store/retrieve configuration variables, query status, etc.

modes_of_operation.name: Backward-frame transmission
modes_of_operation.description: If the executed command was a query (and the address matched), the control gear transmits a single-byte backward frame after a 7×TE..22×TE settling delay.

modes_of_operation.name: Configuration mode (Special Command)
modes_of_operation.description: Entered after INITIALIZE (0xA5); supports addressing assignment via RANDOMIZE/COMPARE/WITHDRAW/SEARCH ADDRESS H,M,L/PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS/VERIFY/QUERY; exited on TERMINATE (0xA1) or after a 15-minute timeout.

modes_of_operation.name: DAPC sequence
modes_of_operation.description: Direct Arc Power Control (command 9 in supported set). Fade rate is bypassed; arc power level is applied directly.

key_features: Two-wire DC bus (typical labels DA+/DA-) for digital control of luminaire fixtures — LED drivers, fluorescent ballasts, emergency lighting, etc.
Polarity-insensitive at receivers — installer can wire either way.
Bus voltage 9.5 V..22.5 V (TI report cites 11.5 V..22.5 V per the standard); bus current capped at ~250 mA.
Manchester-encoded (bi-phase) at 1200 baud — half-bit time TE = 416.67 μs.
Half-duplex with two frame formats: forward (16 bits = start + 8-bit address + 8-bit data + 2 stop) and backward (8 bits = start + 8-bit data + 2 stop).
Up to 64 short (individual) addresses per universe + 16 group addresses + broadcast.
Single-master / multi-slave: control device(s) initiate, control gear (drivers/ballasts) respond.

Logarithmic dimming curve with 254 arc power levels: level 1 = 0.1% illumination, level 254 = 100% illumination, constant 2.8% step between adjacent levels; level 255 = MASK (no change); level 0 = OFF.
Physical Minimum Level (PHYS_MIN_LEVEL) — implementation-defined floor below which the lamp cannot operate; in the TI example 90 (1.17% PWM duty for red and green LEDs at 1.6 kHz).
15 fade times (25 ms..16 s) and 15 fade rates (358 steps/s..2.8 steps/s) controlling smooth Actual-Level transitions to the target arc power.

Address byte format YAAAAAAB: Y=0 → short address 0..63 in AAAAAA; Y=1 → group address 0..15 in AAAA00; Y=1 + AAAAAA=111111 → broadcast; B=0 → direct arc power (8-bit Data is level 0..254 + 255 MASK); B=1 → indirect command in Data byte.

Standard supported indirect commands (direct-arc-power-level commands with B=1): OFF 0x00, UP 0x01, DOWN 0x02, STEP UP 0x03, STEP DOWN 0x04, RECALL MAX LEVEL 0x05, RECALL MIN LEVEL 0x06, STEP DOWN AND OFF 0x07, ON AND STEP UP 0x08, ENABLE DAPC SEQUENCE 0x09, GO TO SCENE 0..15 (0x10..0x1F), RESET 0x20, STORE ACTUAL LEVEL IN DTR 0x21, STORE DTR AS MAX LEVEL—FADE RATE (0x2A..0x2F), STORE DTR AS SCENE 0..15 (0x40..0x4F), REMOVE FROM SCENE 0..15 (0x50..0x5F), ADD TO GROUP 0..15 (0x60..0x6F), REMOVE FROM GROUP 0..15 (0x70..0x7F), STORE DTR AS SHORT ADDRESS 0x80, QUERY STATUS 0x90, QUERY BALLAST 0x91, QUERY LAMP FAILURE 0x92, QUERY LAMP POWER ON 0x93, QUERY LIMIT ERROR 0x94, QUERY RESET STATE 0x95, QUERY MISSING SHORT ADDRESS 0x96, QUERY VERSION NUMBER 0x97, QUERY CONTENT DTR 0x98, QUERY DEVICE TYPE 0x99, READ MEMORY LOCATION 0xC5, STORE DTR AS FAST FADE TIME 0xE4.

Special commands (broadcast, Address byte = 0xA1/0xA3/0xA5... — high nibble pattern 1010xxx1): TERMINATE 0xA1, DTR 0xA3, INITIALIZE 0xA5, RANDOMIZE 0xA7, COMPARE 0xA9, WITHDRAW 0xAB, SEARCH ADDRESS H/M/L 0xB1/0xB3/0xB5, PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS 0xB7, VERIFY SHORT ADDRESS 0xB9, QUERY SHORT ADDRESS 0xBB, PHYSICAL SELECTION 0xBD, ENABLE DEVICE TYPE X 0xC1, DTR1 0xC3, DTR2 0xC5, WRITE MEMORY LOCATION 0xC7.
Required forward-frame inter-frame settling time: ≥ 22×TE (9.17 ms) for the next forward frame; backward frame must start 7×TE..22×TE after the end of the corresponding forward frame.
Cable: 2-wire untwisted, typical 1.5 mm² gauge, up to ~300 m bus length.

Compliant LED control gear must implement IEC 62386-101 (system), -102 (control gear) and the lamp-type-specific part (IEC 62386-207 LED driver / -209 LED module are the LED-relevant ones; the TI report cites IEC 62383-102 / -107 which is an alternative numbering from the bibliography).
transaction_summary: A control device initiates by sending a forward frame (1 start + 8-bit address byte + 8-bit data byte + 2 stop = 16 transmitted Manchester bits + framing). All control gear on the bus receive it; only the addressed control gear (matching short address, group, broadcast, or special selection) acts on it. If the command is a query, the addressed control gear responds 7×TE..22×TE later with a backward frame (1 start + 8-bit data + 2 stop). The control device must wait at least 22×TE (9.17 ms) before sending the next forward frame; a settling time of ≥ 13.5 ms between consecutive forward frames is recommended by IEC 62386.
data_model_summary: Address byte YAAAAAAB — Y selects address mode (short / group / special); AAAAAA selects address index; B selects payload type (direct level vs command).
Direct arc power level 0..254 (logarithmic; level 0 = OFF, level 254 = 100%); 255 = MASK (do not change).
Actual Level — 1 byte in RAM, the current output level of the control gear; updated by direct-arc-power commands and by fade routines.

Configuration variables persisted in flash (information memory): Power On Level, System Failure Level, Minimum Level, Maximum Level, Fade Rate, Fade Time, Short Address, Group membership 0..15 (2 bytes), Scene levels 0..15 (16 bytes), Random Address (3 bytes), Fast Fade Time, Failure Status, Operating Mode, Dimming Curve.
overview: DALI is the IEC-standardized 2-wire bus for digital control of lighting fixtures — LED drivers, fluorescent ballasts, emergency lighting and other luminaire-resident 'control gear'. A control device (panel, sensor, gateway) addresses up to 64 short addresses + 16 group addresses + broadcast per bus universe and sends 16-bit forward frames (1 start + 8-bit address + 8-bit data + 2 stop) Manchester-encoded at 1200 baud. The address byte (YAAAAAAB) selects a single short-address gear, a group, or broadcast and chooses between a direct arc-power level (B=0; data byte is the 254-level logarithmic dimming code with 255 reserved as MASK) and an indirect command (B=1; data byte is a command code such as OFF, UP, DOWN, STEP UP, GO TO SCENE n, STORE DTR AS SHORT ADDRESS, QUERY STATUS, RESET, etc.). For queries the addressed control gear returns an 8-bit backward frame after a 7..22 TE settling time. Special configuration commands (TERMINATE, DTR, INITIALIZE, RANDOMIZE, COMPARE, WITHDRAW, SEARCH ADDRESS H/M/L, PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS, etc.) form a separate command stream used for installation/commissioning — assigning short addresses, programming groups, configuring scenes, and updating persistent variables in flash. The TI SLAA422A application report shows a complete control-gear implementation: the MSP430F2131 (or MSP430G2xx2 in Appendix B) bit-bangs the Manchester decoder on an interrupt-on-edge GPIO pin, uses Timer_A3 to drive two LED PWMs (1.6 kHz, with a 5000-count period that gives a 2.8% step across all 254 levels), and uses the Watchdog Timer Plus interval mode (≈1 ms tick) for fade-rate generation and flash-update housekeeping.

process_technology: Not a silicon part. The MSP430F2131 referenced in the TI application report is a flash microcontroller in the MSP430F2xxx Value-Line family; Appendix B re-targets the implementation to the MSP430G2xx2 value-line devices on the Launchpad MSP-EXP430G2. The DALI bus side uses opto-isolators (e.g. 6N137-class) for galvanic isolation from the bus.
use_cases: Architectural / commercial lighting control — addressable luminaire dimming, scene recall, group control.
Office and conference-room presence/daylight control gateways.
Building Management System (BMS) integration via DALI ↔ KNX / BACnet / Modbus / Ethernet gateways.
LED driver and fluorescent ballast control (IEC 62386-207 LED driver, IEC 62386-209 LED module, IEC 62386-208 colour control DT8, IEC 62386-201 fluorescent ballast).
Tunable-white and colour-changing fixtures via the DT8 colour control (IEC 62386-209).
Outdoor area lighting and street-lighting cabinets.
Sensor-driven occupancy/daylight harvesting via DALI-2 input devices (IEC 62386-303 occupancy sensor / -304 light sensor).
